name: Facet
text: Ship EXCAVA with system preference as the default dark mode, with a persistent one-time theme picker at first launch. This balances user control with immediate familiarity—dark mode reduces eye strain in low light, which aligns with our goal of liveliness and clarity. The trade-off is that users who prefer light mode must manually switch once, but this is a one-time friction that preserves consistency for the majority.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Defaulting to system preference still risks users who prefer light mode in low light—eye strain isn’t just about darkness. A one-time picker at first launch forces a decision users may ignore, but it’s the only way to respect individual preference without guessing wrong. Settle it: test both—track drop-off rates for users who override the default versus those who don’t.

name: Facet
text:
Ship EXCAVA with system preference as the default dark mode, but add a persistent theme toggle in the top-right corner that remembers the user’s choice forever. This keeps the initial load familiar and reduces eye strain for most users, while giving power users full control without cluttering the first launch. The trade-off is a tiny bit of extra UI space, but it’s worth it for the clarity and user satisfaction it delivers.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A persistent toggle still risks users who never notice it—dark mode defaults won’t save them from eye strain in bright light, and a hidden toggle doesn’t solve the core problem. Test a *first-launch picker* with a "remember my choice" checkbox, then log how often users change it later. If >20% adjust within a week, the toggle is worth keeping; if not, scrap it.
